summary: S.T.A.R. (Scientific Terrain Analysis and Recognition) is a Rust-based desktop application designed to analyze and characterize planetary terrain using digital elevation models (DEMs). details:
What the Project Does

S.T.A.R. (Scientific Terrain Analysis and Recognition) is a desktop application designed to characterize planetary landscapes using digital elevation models (DEMs). Users can load GeoTIFF elevation data, inspect raster metadata, validate coordinate reference systems, and analyze terrain morphology.

The application extracts quantitative terrain features, including elevation, slope, local relief, surface roughness, and curvature-related characteristics. Its multiscale analysis examines terrain properties at different spatial scales, helping reveal morphological patterns that may not be apparent from elevation alone. S.T.A.R. also provides terrain visualization through elevation maps, profiles, and distributions, supports batch processing, evaluates data quality, and exports structured JSON results for further analysis.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Planetary terrain analysis is essential for understanding the surfaces of the Moon and Mars. S.T.A.R. aims to make this process more systematic, measurable, and reproducible.

Its long-term goal is to support the identification and comparison of terrestrial terrain analogs — locations on Earth whose surface characteristics resemble those of other planetary bodies. Such comparisons may help researchers understand unfamiliar landscapes, investigate geological similarities, and support future planetary exploration planning.

By combining terrain analysis and visualization in one application, S.T.A.R. provides a foundation for more accessible geospatial research.

Technology and Tools

The application is developed in Rust (Edition 2024). Its native desktop interface is built with eframe and egui. GeoTIFF raster processing uses the tiff crate, while rfd provides native file selection. Cargo is used for dependency management, building, and testing. GitHub is used for source-code management and collaboration.

The project is designed around digital elevation data and modular processing components, allowing additional datasets and analytical methods to be integrated in the future.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The main creative aspect of S.T.A.R. is the combination of geospatial raster processing, quantitative terrain characterization, multiscale analysis, and interactive visualization in a single desktop workflow.

An important design consideration is data reliability. The application accounts for raster dimensions, spatial resolution, coordinate reference systems, measurement units, data coverage, and data quality. These factors are essential because terrain measurements from different sources cannot be compared reliably without considering their spatial and technical characteristics.

The project also includes synthetic DEM generation, allowing developers to test processing and analysis workflows independently of real scientific observations.

S.T.A.R. is currently a working research prototype. Fully automated Earth–Moon–Mars analog ranking, comprehensive planetary dataset integration, and advanced thermal and temporal analysis remain future development goals.
